newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares pause technical rebound, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares pause technical rebound, seen in range.

text.p: Greek stocks were unable to build on a strong open on Thursday and ended a two-day, 100-point rebound with market participants saying current trading patterns were purely technical.

"Today's downturn was clearly based on technical considerations after the market bounced back from the strong 1,450-point support level," said Stathis Nazos, general manager of ABN-AMRO Bank's asset management.
"In the past two days, the market reacted to oversold levels and has now returned to normal conditions, tradewise," he added.
Equities were seen entering a trading range before a new round of appreciation gets under way.

"Easing to 1,450, the market realised a sizeable 38 percent correction of this year's rally to 1,750-points, helping a base-building," Nazos said. "The market is in a trading range, before it resumes its uptrend." he added.
The Athens general index lost 0.86 percent or 13.20 points to 1,530.34 from Thursday's 1,521.88, having fluctuated between 1,552 and 1,515 points.
Turnover amounted to 40.8 billion drachmas on volume of 20.5 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 118 to 91 with 32 shares unchanged on 118 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.25-$11.60. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,105-1,135 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,088-1,148 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument were off 150 drachmas at 6,300.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 520.99-554.25 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.94-$72.63. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,036-3,250 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.38-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 206-236 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
